{"id": "b8c574d3-650c-49e9-88d8-0a9c12f8aedc", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Two of the three checks come out as failing. I couldn't verify what "AWS-1" refers to, so I haven't given it a status.

| Check | Status | Why |
|---|---|---|
| CIS EKS Benchmark 2.1.1 (Enable audit logs) | **FAIL** | The control requires the `audit` control plane log type to be exported to CloudWatch, and your config has it disabled. |
| PCI DSS 10.2.1 (audit logs capture individual user access and actions) | **FAIL (non-compliant)** | The Kubernetes audit log is the only EKS control plane log that records who did what through the API server. `api` and `authenticator` don't cover that. This mapping is my interpretation, not an official AWS-published one. |
| Supplementary check AWS-1 | **Not assessed** | I couldn't find a published definition of it in the AWS documentation. |

**Notes on the result**
- The `api` log is the API server's operational log, and `authenticator` logs authentication events. Neither records per-request user actions. Having them on doesn't make up for audit being off.
- Because `audit` is off, 10.2.1 fails regardless of what the other log types show.
- Only the log-type setting is in scope here. I didn't evaluate CloudWatch retention (PCI DSS 10.5.1 expects at least 12 months), log integrity, or access controls on the log group.

**To fix both failures:** enable the `audit` log type on the cluster. The `eksctl` command is `eksctl utils update-cluster-logging --enable-types audit --approve`, or you can update the cluster's logging config directly. CloudWatch ingestion and storage costs will go up.

If you paste the definition of AWS-1 or tell me which tool it comes from, I'll give it a status. If it just means "all control plane log types enabled", it would also fail, since `scheduler` and `controllerManager` aren't enabled either. I'd treat that as a guess, not a result.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
